translations.text: In the month of Kanun, in the twentieth year, I was staying in Susa the citadel.
Hanani, one of my brothers, came with some Jewish men. I asked them about the Jews who remained from the captivity, and also about the city of Jerusalem.

These men whom I questioned said to me, “Those people who escaped from captivity are there in the city, living in great distress and deep disgrace. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire.”
When I heard these words, I sat down and wept and mourned for many days. I fasted and prayed before the God of heaven.
I said, “I beg you, LORD, God of heaven, mighty, great, and awesome God, who preserves faithfulness and kindness toward those who love him and keep his commandments:

Let your eyes now be open and your ears attentive to hear the prayer that I, your servant, pray before you day and night for the Israelites, your servants. I confess the sins that the Israelites have committed against you. Both I and my father’s household have sinned before you.
We have not kept the commandments and laws that you commanded your servant Moses.
Remember the words you commanded your servant Moses, when you told him, ‘If you are unfaithful to me, I will scatter you among the nations.

But if you return to me and keep my laws and carry them out, even if your scattered people are at the ends of heaven, I will bring you back from there and bring you to the place I have chosen for my name to dwell.’
They are your servants and your people, whom you redeemed by your great power and your strong hand.

I beg you, LORD, let your ear be attentive to the prayer of your servant and to the prayer of those who desire to fear your name. Deliver your servant today, and grant him compassion in this man’s presence.” Now I was cupbearer to the king.
Then, in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, I was serving wine before the king. I took the wine and gave it to the king. I had not been sad in his presence.
The king said to me, “Why is your face sad, when you are not sick? This can only be sadness of heart.” I was very frightened.
I said to the king, “May the king live forever! Why should my face not be sad, when the city of my ancestors’ royal house lies in ruins and its gates have been burned with fire?”
And the king spoke to me about this. I pleaded and prayed before the God of heaven.
I said to the king, “If it pleases the king, I am your servant before you. Send me to Judah, to the city of David, to the burial place of my ancestors, so that I may rebuild it.”
The king said to me, “Fool, how long will you be going and returning?” It pleased the king, and he sent me and gave me a set time.
I said to the king, “If it pleases the king, let letters be written for me to the governors beyond the River, so that they will assist me until I reach Judah,

and a letter to Asaph, keeper of the king’s park, so that he will give me timber to make the gates of the house, of the houses, and of the city wall, and for the house I will enter.” The king granted this to me, because the hand of my God had been good to me.
I came to the governor beyond the River and gave him the king’s letter. The king had sent army officers and horsemen with me.
Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah, the Ammonite men, heard about this. They were deeply displeased that someone had come to seek the welfare of the Israelites.
I came to Jerusalem and stayed there for three days.
I got up at night, along with the men who were with me. I had not told anyone what God had put into my heart to do for Jerusalem. There was no animal with me except the animal I was riding.
I went out at night through the Valley Gate toward the Dragon Spring and the Dung Gate. I inspected the walls of Jerusalem, which were broken down, and the gates, which had been burned with fire.
I passed by the Valley Gate and the king’s canal, but there was no room for the animal to pass through there.
I went up through the valley at night, inspecting the wall. Then I came back, entered through the Valley Gate, and returned.
The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing. Until then I had told nothing to the Jews, the priests, the officials, the scribes, or the rest of those doing the work.
And I said to them, “You see the trouble we are in: Jerusalem is in ruins, and its gates are burned with fire. Come, let us rebuild Jerusalem’s wall, so that we will no longer be a disgrace.”

I told them about the hand of my God, which had been with me for good, and also about the words the king had spoken to me. They said, “Let us rise and build.” And they strengthened their hands to do what was good.
When Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite man, and Geshem the Arab heard, they laughed at us and mocked us, saying, “What is this thing you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?”
I answered them, saying, “The God of heaven himself will save us. We are working, rising up, and building. But you have no right, memorial, or share in Jerusalem.”

Eliashib the high priest rose, together with his fellow priests and his sons, at the Garden Gate. They installed its doors and consecrated it. They consecrated it as far as the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Tower of Hananel.
And as far as the boundary of the men of Jericho, and as far as the boundary of the sons of Zebur, Imri [?].
The sons of Senaah built the Fish Gate. They put it in order and installed its doors, its bolts, and its bars.

Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired as far as the boundary. Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshizkel, repaired as far as the boundary. Zadok son of Baana repaired as far as the boundary.
The Tekoites and their officials repaired as far as the boundary, but they did not put their necks to the service of their masters.
Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Beseriah repaired the Gate of the Two. They put it in order and installed its doors, its bolts, and its bars.
Melatiah the Gibeonite and Nadon the Merathite repaired as far as the boundary. The men of Gibeon and Mizpah made a seat for the governor of the region Beyond the River.
Uzziel son of Hadaiah, son of a goldsmith, repaired the boundary. Hananiah son of [?] repaired the boundary. They left Jerusalem with its wall widened.
Jeremiah son of Hur, ruler of Jerusalem, repaired the boundary.
Jedaiah son of Harumaph and the head of his household strengthened the adjoining section, and Hattush son of Hashabneiah strengthened the adjoining section.
Malchijah son of Harim and Hashum son of the ruler of Moab repaired a second stretch and the tower that remained.
Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of Jerusalem, repaired as far as the boundary, he and his sons.
Hanun, an inhabitant of Zioah, repaired the Valley Gate. They built it and installed its doors, its bolts, and its bars. There were a thousand cubits of wall as far as the Refuse Gate.
Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of Beth-haccherem, repaired the Refuse Gate. They built it and installed its doors, its bolts, and its bars.

Shallum son of Hozah, ruler of Mizpah, repaired the Spring Gate. They built it, roofed it, and installed its doors, its bolts, and its bars. They also repaired the wall of the pool that supplies water to the king’s garden, as far as the stairway descending from the City of David.
After him, Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of Beth-zur, repaired as far as the path to David’s tomb, as far as the constructed pool, and as far as the House of the Warriors.
After him, the Levite Rehum son of Bani reinforced the wall as far as the boundary of Hashabiah, ruler of the entrance.
After him, their brothers reinforced the wall: Buzzi son of Hadar, ruler of Keilah.
He reinforced a second stretch as far as the boundary of Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, opposite the stairway leading to the corner.
After him, Baruch son of Zaccai took up the work and reinforced a second stretch as far as the corner and as far as the entrance to the house of Eliashib the high priest.
After him, Meremoth son of Uriah, of Hakkoz, reinforced a second stretch from the entrance to Eliashib’s house as far as the end of Eliashib’s house.
After him, the priests, the men of the valley, reinforced the wall.
After him, Benjamin and Hasshub, the head of his household, made repairs. After him, Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, made repairs behind his house.
After him, Bazzui son of Henadad repaired a second section, from Azariah’s house as far as the middle and as far as the corner.

Of Palal son of Uzai, opposite the corner and as far as the tower of the plain that projects from the king’s upper residence, and as far as the courtyard of the prison. After him, Peraiah son of Parosh.
And the temple servants who lived in Ophel, as far as the Water Gate on the east and the projecting tower.
After him, the people of Tekoa repaired a second section, from opposite the great projecting tower as far as the fortified wall.
From the entrance of the Horse Gate, the priests made repairs, each opposite his own house.
After them, Zadok son of Immer made repairs opposite his house. After him, Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the East Gate, made repairs.

After him, Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired a second section. After him, Meshullam son of Berechiah made repairs opposite his house. After him, Binnui son of Henadad repaired a second section.
After him, Malchijah son of a goldsmith made repairs as far as the house of the temple servants and the merchants, opposite the Exit Gate, and as far as the ascent at the corner.
Between the ascent at the corner and the [?] Gate, the goldsmiths and merchants made repairs.
When Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he was upset and became very angry, and he mocked the Jews.

He said to his brothers and the army of the Samaritans, “What are the Jews doing, boasting? Let them offer sacrifices and eat on the day they set up these stones from the heap of dirt, even though the stones are burned.”
Tobiah the Ammonite was standing beside him and said, “However much they build, I know that a fox will climb up and dislodge the stones of their walls.”
Hear, our God, because we have become a laughingstock. Turn their insults back on their own heads, and give them over to plunder in the land of their captivity.
Do not forgive their offenses, and do not let their sins be wiped away from before you, because they have raged against the construction we are doing.
And we will build the wall. They built it, and the wall was completed to half its height. Then the mouth of all the people was opened to work.

Then, when Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people of Ashdod heard that time had been given for Jerusalem’s wall to be rebuilt and that the breaches were beginning to be closed, they were very upset.
They all plotted together to come and fight against Jerusalem and cause trouble for its people.
We prayed before God that he would set guards over us by day and by night to protect us from them.
The Jews said, “The basket carriers have lost their strength, and there is far too much rubble. We cannot build the wall.”
Our enemies said, “They will neither know nor see until we fall upon them, kill them, and put a stop to their work.”
The Jews who lived near them came and told us, “Look, by now they have come ten times to fight against you, from all the places where they were scattered.”
They came and stood behind the wall to fight against you with their arrows, and they divided the army into clans, with their swords, spears, and bows.

I was afraid, and I stood up and said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and fearsome, and fight for your brothers, your sons, and your daughters.”
Then, when our enemies heard that the matter had become known to us and that the Lord had nullified their promises, we all returned and went up to the wall, and each of us worked at his own task.
And half of the young men—from that day onward, half of the people did the work, and half held spears, shields, bows, and armor. The attendants stood behind the Jews.
They were building the wall, and those carrying loads in baskets carried them while working with one hand and holding a weapon with the other.
Each builder held a sword and stood building, and the man who sounded the horn stood behind him.
I said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, “The work is extensive and spread out, and we stand scattered along the wall, separated from one another.
Wherever you hear the sound of the horn, gather there with us, and our God will fight for us.”
We will continue doing our work, while half of us hold spears from the first light of dawn until the stars come out.
At that time I also told the people that each man and his servant should spend the night in the streets of Jerusalem, guarding it by night and by day and doing the work.
Neither I nor my brothers, my servants, or the guards who followed me took off our clothes for a full month—each man who reached him [?].
Then the people and their wives raised a loud outcry against their fellow Jews.
Some were saying, “Our sons, our daughters, and our brothers are many. Let us get grain so that we can eat and live.”
Others were saying, “We are selling our fields, houses, and vineyards to get grain during the famine and stay alive.”
Others were saying, “Let us borrow money from the king’s tax, cultivate our fields and vineyards, and live.”

Others were saying, “Now our flesh is like the flesh of our brothers, and our children are like their children. Yet here we are subjecting our sons and daughters to slavery, and some of our daughters are being subjected to service as slave women. They do not raise their hands before God, and our fields, vineyards, and possessions are being given to others.”
I was deeply distressed when I heard their outcry and these words.
My heart was broken within me, but I controlled my temper and spoke with the elders and the nobles.

I told them, “We are buying our fellow Jews who are being sold to the nations, both them and their children, yet each of you is taking his own brother.” Because of this I raised my voice against them and said, “Will you too sell your brothers?” They were silent and gave me no answer.
I said to them, “What you are doing is not good. You are not living in the fear of our God, since you are acting like the nations around us.
Let me, my sons, and my brothers also take money, buy grain, and leave it for the poor among our people.
Let us return their fields, vineyards, olive trees, and houses to them, and let us leave the money, grain, wine, and oil for the rest of the people.”
They said to me, “We will do as you say.” I summoned the priests and told them that this was what ought to be done, and I made them swear to act according to this promise.

And also to the boys [?]. They said, “May God likewise shake out from his house and from his labor every man who does not keep this promise. May he likewise be shaken out and left empty.” All the people said, “Amen.” All the people stood up and praised the Lord, and all the people acted according to this promise.

Also, from the day he appointed me governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes, twelve years, I was their leader along with my brothers. I did not take a donkey from any one of them, nor did I harass any of them.

The governors before me had subjected the people and taken wine, bread, and much money from them as tribute, as much as forty shekels. They also gave their servants power over the people, and these exercised authority over them and mistreated them. But I did not act that way, because I feared God.
I also devoted myself vigorously to the work on this wall, and I bought no fields. All the young Jewish men gathered and stood there at the work.
The nobles and officials numbered one hundred and fifty men, and those who came to us from the nations around us came to us, each man at his table.

The man who prepared the food would bring one ox and six fat sheep to the laborers who were working, and birds were prepared for us. Once every ten days there was wine in abundance. Yet despite this, I did not seek food or authority, because the work weighed heavily on this people.
Remember me for good, my God, for everything I have done for this people.

Then Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that I had rebuilt the wall and that no breach remained in it, although up to that time the gateposts had not yet been set up.
Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, “Come, let us go together and camp as a company in the plain of Ono.” But they were planning to harm me.
I sent a messenger to them and said, “I am doing a great work and cannot come down. Why should it stop while I leave it and come down to you?”
They sent me this same message four times, and I gave them the same answer.
Sanballat sent his servant to me a fifth time with the same message and a letter in his hand.

It was written in it: “It has been reported among the nations, and Geshem says, that you and the Jews are planning to rebel. That is why you are building the wall, and according to these reports you are to become their king.
You have also appointed prophets to prophesy about you in Jerusalem, saying, ‘Look, Ezra has become king in Judah!’ Now the king will hear reports like these. So come, let us take counsel together.”
I sent to him and said, “Things are not as you say. You are saying these things out of your own imagination.”
For they were all trying to frighten us, saying, “Their hands will grow weak and stop working,” and telling us not to do the work. Now strengthen my hands!

I went into the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel. He was confined there, and he said to me, “Come, let us meet in the house of the Lord, inside the temple, and shut the temple doors, because they are coming to kill you. They are coming at night to kill you.”
I said, “Should a man like me run away? Far be it from me to run away and enter the temple!”

But I knew that God had not sent him against me, nor had it been said to me through a prophet that he would kill me. Tobiah, Sanballat, and his companions had hired him and sent him against me to kill me.
For he was hired so that I would become afraid, act in this way, and sin, and so that they would have grounds to give me a bad name and reproach me.
Remember, my God, Tobiah, Sanballat, and his companions according to these hateful deeds of theirs. Remember also Jodaiah the prophet and the rest of the prophets who were making me afraid of them.
The wall was finished on the twenty-fifth of Elul, in fifty-two days.
Then, when all our enemies heard, all the nations around us became afraid and trembled greatly before us. They knew that this work had been accomplished by God.
Also in those days the nobles of the Jews sent many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah’s letters came to them.

For there were many people in Judah who had sworn to him that they would not oppose him, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
They also spoke of his good words in my presence, and they reported to him whatever I said. Tobiah himself sent letters to frighten me.
Then, when the wall had been built, the gates were standing, the gateposts had been set up, and the gatekeepers, attendants, and Levites had been organized,
I put my brother Hanani and Hananiah, the governor of the citadel of Jerusalem, in charge, because he was an upright man who feared God and turned away from evil.

I said to them, “The gates of Jerusalem must not be opened until the sun is up. While it is still daylight, the gates must be shut and secured. The inhabitants of Jerusalem must stand guard, each at his post and each opposite his own house.”
The city was large and spacious, but there were few people in it, and they had no houses built.

My God put it into my heart, and I gathered the free men and the nobles of the people according to their families. I found the genealogical record of those who had come up at first, and I found written in it:
These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity of the exile, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had deported. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town.
Those who came up with Zerubbabel were Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nehemiael, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
The descendants of Parosh: two thousand one hundred seventy-two.
The descendants of Shephatiah: 372.
The descendants of Arah: 652.
The descendants of Pahath-moab, belonging to the descendants of Jeshua and Joab: 2,818.
The descendants of Elam: 1,254.
The descendants of Zattu: 854.
The descendants of Zaccai: 760.
The descendants of Bani: 644.
The descendants of Bebai: 628.
The descendants of Azgad: 2,322.
The descendants of Adonikam: 667.
The descendants of Bigvai: 2,067.
The descendants of Adin: 655.
The descendants of Ater, of Hezekiah's family: 98.
The descendants of Hashum: 328.
The descendants of Bezai: 324.
The descendants of Huram: 112.
The descendants of Gibeon: 95.
The men of Bethlehem and Netophah: 188.
The men of Anathoth: 128.
The men of Beth-armuth: 42.
The men of Beth-nearin, Chephirah, and Beeroth: 743.
The men of Geba and Ramah: 721.
The men of Michmash: 122.
The men of Bethel and Ai: 123.
The men of Nebo: 52.
Those of the house of Elam: 1,254.
The descendants of Harim: 320.
The descendants of Jericho: three hundred and forty-five.
The descendants of Lod and Ono: 721.
The descendants of Senaah: 3,930.
The priests: the descendants of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua: 973.
The descendants of Immer: 1,052.
The descendants of Pashhur: 1,247.
The descendants of Hadum: 1,017.
The Levites, the descendants of Jeshua belonging to Kadmiel, of the descendants of Hodiah: 74.
The ministers, the descendants of Asaph: 148.
And the gatekeepers: the descendants of Shallum, the descendants of Ater, the descendants of Talmon, the descendants of Akkub, the descendants of Hatita, and the descendants of Shobai: 138.
The men: the descendants of Ziha, the descendants of Hasupha, and the descendants of Tabbaoth.
The descendants of Keros, the descendants of Sia, and the descendants of Peron.
The descendants of Lebana, the descendants of Hagaba, and the descendants of Shalmai.
The descendants of Hanani, the descendants of Adda, and the descendants of Hagar.
The descendants of Ana, the descendants of Rezin, and the descendants of Dekora.
The descendants of Gazzam, the descendants of Adda, and the descendants of Paseah.
The descendants of Besai, the descendants of Meunim, and the descendants of Japhusin.
The descendants of Bakbuk, the descendants of Hakupha, and the descendants of Harhur.
The descendants of Bazluth, the descendants of Mehida, and the descendants of Harsha.
The descendants of Bazuk, the descendants of Sisera, and the descendants of Temah.
The descendants of Neziah and the descendants of Hatipha.
The descendants of Solomon’s servants: the descendants of Sotai, the descendants of Sophereth, and the descendants of Peruiah.
The descendants of Jaala, the descendants of Darkon, and the descendants of Giddel.
The descendants of Shephatiah, the descendants of Hattil, the descendants of Cabroth, the descendants of Zebaim, and the descendants of Amon.
All the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon’s servants: 392.
These came up from Tel-melah to Tel-abba and Cherub. They spoke, but could not show their ancestral families or their lineage, except that they were from Israel.
The descendants of Bani, the descendants of Delaiah, the descendants of Tobiah, and the descendants of Dekora: 642.

And from the priests: the descendants of Hananiah, the descendants of Hakkoz, and the descendants of Barzillai, who took a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
These men searched for their names in the record of their family lines but did not find them, and they were excluded from the priesthood.
The elders of the priests told them not to eat any of the most holy food until a high priest arose who could inquire and discern.
The whole assembly together numbered 42,470.
Besides these were their male and female slaves, who numbered 7,333 in all, and 245 male and female attendants.
There were 435 camels and 6,720 donkeys.
Some of the family heads gave for the work on the house. The elders of the priests gave to the treasury 1,000 gold darics, 50 bowls, and 530 tunics for the priests.
Some of the family heads gave to the treasury for the work 20,000 gold darics and 2,200 minas of silver.
The rest of the people gave 20,000 gold darics, 2,000 minas of silver, and 67 tunics for the priests.

The priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the attendants, some of the people, the temple servants, and all Israel returned to their towns. When the seventh month arrived, the Israelites were in their towns.
All the people gathered as one in the square in front of the Water Gate. They told Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the Law of Moses, which the LORD had commanded Israel to follow.
On the first day of the seventh month, Ezra the priest brought the book of the Law before the people, both men and women, and everyone who was ready to listen.

He read the book in the square at the Water Gate from morning until noon, before the men and women and those who could listen. The people inclined their ears and listened attentively to the commandments of the Law.

Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform that he had made so that he could speak from it. Beside him on his right stood Mattithiah, Shemua, Ananiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah. On his left stood Peraiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashabiah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
Ezra the scribe opened the book of the Law in the sight of all the people, for he was above all the people. When he opened it, all the people stood up.
Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God, and all the people answered, saying, “Amen and amen!” They raised their hands, then bowed down and worshiped before the LORD with their faces to the ground.

Jeshua and his sons, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabar, Hanani, Penaiah, and the Levites were serving the people in matters of the Law, while the people stood in their places.
They read from the book of the Law of the LORD as it lay open, and the people were instructed in it and understood what was read.

Nehemiah, the chief of the priests, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were ministering to the people spoke to all the people, saying, “Today is holy before the Lord your God. Do not grieve or weep.” For all the people were weeping as they heard the book of the law.

He said to them, “Go, eat and drink, and send food to anyone who has nothing prepared, because today is holy before the LORD. Do not grieve, because it is a day of rejoicing in the LORD, and he will be your helper.”
The Levites quieted all the people, saying, “Be quiet, because today is holy, and do not weep.”
All the people went to eat and drink, to send food, and to celebrate with great joy, because they had understood the words that had been made known to them.
On the second day, the family heads of all the people, together with the priests and Levites, gathered around Ezra the scribe to receive instruction from him about the book of the Law.
They found in the book of the Law that the LORD had commanded Moses that the Israelites should live in shelters during the festival in the month of Tishri.

To make this known, they had heralds proclaim throughout all their towns and in Jerusalem, saying, “Go up to the mountain and bring branches of olive trees and walnut trees, palm leaves, citron leaves, and willow branches. Make shelters, as it is written in the book of the Law of Moses.”

The people went out, brought the branches, and made shelters for themselves, each on his roof and in their courtyards, in the courtyard of the house of the LORD, in the square at the Water Gate, and in the square at the Ephraim Gate.

All the people who had returned from captivity made shelters and lived in them. The Israelites had not done this since the days of Joshua son of Nun until that very day, and there was exceedingly great joy.

They read from the book of the law of the Lord every day, from the first day to the last day. They celebrated the festival for seven days, and on the eighth day they assembled, as it was prescribed for them.
On the twenty-fourth day of this same month, the Israelites assembled, fasting and wearing sackcloth, and put ashes on themselves.
The descendants of Israel separated themselves from all the other peoples. They stood and confessed their sins and the sins of their ancestors.

They stood in their places and read from the book of the law of the Lord their God. For a quarter of the day they read, and for a quarter of the day they confessed and bowed down before the Lord their God.
The leaders over the Levites stood up: Jeshua and Kadmiel, the sons of Hashabiah, and Sherebiah, the sons of Chenani. They prayed aloud before the Lord their God.

The Levites—Jeshua and Kadmiel, the sons of Hashabiah, and Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shecaniah, and Pethahiah—said, “Stand up and bless the Lord their God from everlasting to everlasting. Blessed is his glorious name, exalted above all created things and all praises.

You alone are the Lord. You made heaven, the highest heavens and all their armies, the earth and everything on it, and the waters and everything in them. You give life to them all, and the armies of heaven bow down to you.
You are the Lord God who chose Abram, brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans, and changed his name to Abraham.

You found his heart pure before you and swore oaths to him to give him the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, Jebusites, and Girgashites—to give it to his descendants. You fulfilled your words to him, because you are righteous.
You saw the enslavement of our ancestors in Egypt and heard their outcry at the Red Sea.

You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, all his army, and all the people of his land, because you knew that they had acted arrogantly toward your people. You made a name for yourself that remains to this day.
You split the sea before them, and they crossed through the sea on dry ground. You drowned their pursuers in the depths of the sea, as a stone sinks in mighty waters.
You led them by a pillar of cloud during the day and by a pillar of fire at night, to light the way for them to walk.
You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven. You gave them just judgments, true laws, and good statutes and commandments.
You made your holy Sabbath known to them, along with the commandments, statutes, and laws that you commanded them through your servant Moses.
You gave them bread from heaven for their hunger and water from the rock for their thirst. You told them to enter and take possession of the land that your hand had prepared to give them.
But they and their ancestors acted arrogantly, became stubborn, and did not obey your commandments.

They refused to listen and did not remember the wonders you had done for them. Their hearts turned back to their evil deeds. But you are a forgiving, compassionate, and gracious God, slow to anger and ready to hear prayer. You did not abandon them.
For they made a cast-metal calf and said, “This is your God, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt,” and they committed great evils.

In your great mercy you did not abandon them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not depart from them by day, guiding them along the way, nor did the pillar of fire by night, lighting the path they were to take.
You gave your good Spirit to teach them. You did not withhold manna from their mouths, and you gave them water for their thirst.
For forty years you deprived them of nothing in the wilderness. Their clothes did not wear out, and their sandals did not split.
You gave them the kingdoms of the nations and allotted portions to them individually. They took possession of the land of Sihon, the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og, king of Bashan.
You made their children as numerous as the stars in heaven and brought them into the land that you had told their ancestors to enter and possess.

Their children entered and took possession of the land. You crushed before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and handed them over to them, along with their kings and the peoples of the land, to do with them as they pleased.

They captured fortified towns and fertile land. They took possession of houses filled with every good thing, cisterns already dug, vineyards, olive trees, and abundant fruit trees. They ate, were satisfied, grew fat, and delighted in your great goodness.
But they turned away and were unfaithful to you. They cast your law out of their minds and killed your prophets because they told them to return to you. They committed great evils.

You handed them over to their enemies, who oppressed them. In their time of distress they pleaded with you, and you heard them from heaven in your great compassion. You raised up deliverers for them, who rescued them from the power of their oppressors.

But when you gave them relief, they again did what was hateful in your sight. You abandoned them to their enemies, who enslaved them. Then they again prayed before you, and you heard from heaven and rescued them every time, according to your abundant compassion.

You warned them to turn them back to your laws, but they acted arrogantly and did not obey your commandments. They sinned against your judgments, by which a person will live if he follows them. They turned a rebellious shoulder, stiffened their necks, and would not listen.
You spoke out against them for many years and warned them by your Spirit through your prophets, but they did not listen. So you handed them over to the peoples of the cities.
Yet because of your great mercy you did not destroy them or abandon them, for you are a gracious and merciful God.

Now, our God, the great, mighty, and fearsome God, who keeps oaths and is faithful, do not let all the distress that has come upon us be hidden from your sight—upon us, our kings, our leaders, our priests, our prophets, our ancestors, and all the people, from the days of the king of Assyria until today.
You are just in everything that has come upon us, for you are indeed truthful, while we have acted arrogantly.
Our kings, our leaders, our priests, and our ancestors did not follow your law or heed your commandments and the warnings with which you warned them.
They rejected your kingship and the great goodness you gave them in the good and fertile land you gave them. They did not serve you or turn away from their evil deeds.
Because of this, we are slaves today. As for the land you gave our ancestors so that they could eat its fruit and enjoy its good things, here we are, working within it as slaves.
The kings you appointed over us because of our sins take its produce. They rule over our bodies and our livestock as they please, and we live in great distress.
In all these matters we swear faithfully, and we—our elders, the Levites, and our priests—bear witness to the seal.
And all those of us who survived: Nehemiah the elder, son of Hananiah, the chief priest, and Zerahiah;
and Seraiah, Azariah, and Jeremiah;
and Pashhur, Jeremiah, Malchijah, and Peshtiah;
and Hattush, Shecaniah, and Malluch;
and Shecum, Azmaveth, and Gebariah;
Daniel, Gibbethon, Baruch;
Meshullam, Abijah, Benjamin;
Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah. These were the priests.
And the Levites: Jeshua son of Jezaniah, the sons of Mabbani, Hader the first;
and their brothers: Shecaniah, Uriah, Kelita, Pelatiah, Hanani;
Mica, Rechub, Hashabiah;
Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shecaniah;
Hodiah, the sons of Bani.
The leaders of the people: Parosh, the ruler of Moab, Elam, Zattu;
the sons of Azgar and the sons of Adonijah.
Bigvai, Adin.
Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur.
Uriah, Hashum, Bezai.
Hoziph, Anathoth, Nebai.
Magpiash, Meshullam, Aziphi.
Meshezabel, Zadok, Jehoiada.
Pelatiah, Hanani, Ananiah.
Hoshea, Hananiah, Jeshua.
Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek.
Rehum, Hashabiah, Maaseiah.
Ahijah, Hanani, Anan.
Malluch, Harim, Baanah.

The rest of the people—the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the ministers, the servants, and everyone who had separated themselves from the peoples of the lands—are to come to the law of the Lord, together with their wives, their sons, their daughters, and everyone who knows and understands.

They stand in support of their brothers and relatives and enter into an oath and a covenant to follow the law of the Lord, which was given through Moses, the Lord’s servant, and to observe and carry out all the commandments of the Lord our Lord, his judgments, and his laws.
We will not give our daughters to the peoples of the land or take their daughters as wives for our sons.

They shall not take from the peoples of the land who bring [?]. We will not accept payment from anyone who hires out an animal on the Sabbath day, and we will not carry a load on the Sabbath day, because it is holy. We will cancel everything owed to us; in the seventh year we ourselves will cancel it.
We imposed on ourselves the obligation to give a third of a stater each week for the service of the house of our God.

For the bread set out before God, the regular offerings, the regular burnt offering for the Sabbaths, the new moons, and the festivals, the holy offerings, the forgiveness of Israel’s sins, and all the work of the house of our God.
The priests, the Levites, and the people cast lots concerning the offerings of wood, to bring them to the house of the Lord our God, as it is written in the book of the law.
To bring the first produce of our land and the first of all the fruit of the trees, year after year, and to bring it to the house of the Lord.

The firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, as it is written in the law of the Lord, and the firstborn of our cattle and our flocks, to bring them to the house of our God, to the priests who serve in the house of our God.

We will give the first of our dough, the produce of our threshing floors, the fruit of all our trees, wine, and oil to the priests who serve before our God. We will give a tenth of the produce of our lands to the Levites, and the Levites themselves will collect the tithes from all the villages where we work.
A priest descended from Aaron shall be with the Levites when they collect their tithes, and the Levites shall take a tenth to the house of our God, to the storerooms and the treasury.

For the Israelites and the descendants of Levi shall bring the first produce of grain, wine, and oil to the storerooms. The sacred vessels are there, and the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, and the guards shall not abandon the house of our God.

The elders of the people shall live in Jerusalem, and the rest of the people shall cast lots to bring one person out of every ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city, while the other nine portions shall remain in the villages.
The people blessed all those who willingly chose to live in Jerusalem.

These are the leaders of the province who lived in Jerusalem and in the villages of Judah. Each man lived on his own inherited property in their villages: Israelites, priests, Levites, the people, and the descendants of Solomon’s servants.
In Jerusalem, from the descendants of Judah, Benjamin, and Hodiah: Nethaniah son of Uzziah, son of Zechariah, son of Amariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Mahalalel, from the descendants of Perez.
Maaseiah son of Baruch, son of Col-hozeh, son of Adaiah, son of Azariah, son of Jonadab, son of Zechariah, son of Shelah.
All the descendants of Perez who lived in Jerusalem numbered 468 valiant men.
These are the descendants of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Joiada, son of Peraiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Naasiah, son of Antiel, son of Jeshaiah.
And after him, 928.
Joel son of Zechariah was in charge of them, and Judah son of Senuah was in charge of the city’s second quarter.
From the priests: Berechiah son of Joiada,
and Seraiah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Mericoth, son of Ahitub, who was in charge of the house of the Lord.
His brothers who did the work inside numbered 822. And Azariah son of Jeroham, son of Pelaniah, son of Amzer, son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malchiah.
Their relatives, heads of their ancestral households, numbered 242; and Amashai son of Azarel, son of Ahzai, son of Meshillemoth, son of Immer.
Their brothers, mighty warriors, numbered 128. In charge of them was Zabdiel, son of the nobles.
From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Jeshua, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, son of Bani,
son of Shabbethai; and Jozabar, who was in charge of the outside work of the house of the Lord and was among the leaders of the Levites.
Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zabdi, son of Asaph, the foremost leader of the Jews in prayer; Bakbukah, second among his brothers; and Ira son of Shammua, son of Galal, son of Jethron.
All the Levites in the holy city numbered 284.
And second were Akkub and Talmon and their brothers who guarded the gate, numbering 172.
The rest of Israel, and the priests and Levites, were in all the towns of Judah, each on his own inherited property.
Their servants lived each at his work and on his farmland.

The one in charge of the Levites in Jerusalem was Abdi son of Buni, son of Hashabiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Mica, from the descendants of Asaph, who served in connection with the work of the house of the Lord.
For the king's command applied to them, and a fixed provision was established for those who served, day by day.
Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, from the descendants of Zerah son of Judah, was in charge of everything the king ordered concerning all the people's affairs.
As for their settlements and their fields, some of the descendants of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba and its villages, in Ribon and its villages, and in Kabzeel and its villages;
in Hoshea, Moladah, and Beth-pelet;
in Hazar-shua, Beersheba, and its villages;
in Zankela, Mekiah, and its villages;
in En-rimmon, Zedah, and Jarmuth;
in Zioah, Adullam, and their villages; in Lachish and its villages; and in Azekah and its villages. They settled from Beersheba as far as the Valley of Hinnom.
The descendants of Benjamin were from Ramah of Michmash, Ai, and Bethel and its villages;
Anathoth, Joab, and Ananiah;
Hazor, Ramah, and Gittaim.
And Hadar, Zeboim, and Jeballat.
And Lod, Ono, Niha, and Harsha.
And among the Levites were divisions of Judah and Benjamin.
These are the priests and Levites who came up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua: Seraiah, Azma, Ezra,
Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
Iddo, Azzath, Abijah,
Benjamin, Maadariah, Bilgai,
Shemaiah, Naddub, Jedaiah,
Sallai, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah. These were the heads of the priests and their brothers in the days of Jeshua.
The Levites: Jeshua and his sons, Kadmiel, Arabiah, Judah, Mattaniah, Hodith [?]—he and his brothers.
And Bakbukiah, Eli, and their brothers stood opposite them on watch.
Jeshua fathered Joiakim, Joiakim fathered Eliashib, and Eliashib fathered Joiada.
Joiada fathered Jonathan, and Jonathan fathered Jaddua.
In the days of Joiakim, the priests who were heads of ancestral families were: Seraiah, Amariah, Jeremiah, Hananiah,
Ezra, Meshullam, Amariah, Johanan,
Malchijah, Jonathan, Shecaniah, Joseph,
Harim, Ariah, Meroth, Lahmi,
Iddo, Zechariah, Gaathon, Meshullam,
Abijah, Zichri, Benjamin, Modiah, Pilta,
Bilgah, Shammua, Shemaiah, Jonathan,
Joiada, Mattani, Jedaiah, Uzzi,
Sallai, Kallai, Amok, Ammi,
Hilkiah, Hashabiah, Hoda, Nethanel.
The Levites who were heads of ancestral families in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Joiada were recorded, as were the priests during the reign of Darius the Persian.
The descendants of Levi who were heads of ancestral families were recorded in the book of the daily records down to the days of Johanan son of Eliashib.

The heads of the Levites were Jeshbiel, Sherebiah, and Jeshua, with his brothers, the sons of Kadmiel, opposite them, praising and giving thanks according to the commands of David, the prophet of the Lord, watch opposite watch.
Mattaniah, Bukki, Obadiah, Shallum, Talmon, and Akkub, the gatekeeper.
These were in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiael the leader and Ezra the priest and scribe.
When the wall of Jerusalem was finished, they gathered the Levites from throughout their territory to bring them to Jerusalem and celebrate with rejoicing, thanksgiving, praises, cymbals, and lyres.
The sons of the ministers gathered from the plain around Jerusalem and from the settlement of Netophah,
and from Beth-gilgal, from the valley of Geba, and from Aramoth, because the ministers had built settlements for themselves around Jerusalem.
The priests and Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people and the gates of the wall.
They brought the leaders of Judah up onto the wall and appointed two large assemblies. They walked along the top of the wall to the right, from the Great Gate.
Hoshaiah went with them, along with half the leaders of Judah,
and Azriel, Ezra, and Meshullam,
and Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah,
and some of the sons of the priests with horns: Zechariah son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Maacah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph.

And his brothers Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, [?], Nethanel, Hanani, and Judah, with the musical instruments of David, the prophet and servant of the Lord; and Ezra the scribe went before them.
Above the Fountain Gate, directly opposite them, they went up the ascent of the City of David, along the ascent of the wall, above David’s house, to the great eastern gate.
They gave thanks and went up above, with me behind them. Half the people went up onto the wall and stood at the great tower and on the high wall, above the broad wall.
They went above the Gate of Ephraim as far as the Old Gate and the Fishermen’s Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel as far as the high tower and the Garden Gate. They stood at the Great Gate.
The two assemblies entered the house of the Lord, along with me and half the officials who were with me,
and the priests Eliakim and Maaseiah, [?], Micah, Elihu, Anani, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with horns,
and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Johanan, Malchijah, Elam, Azzur, and Shammua, the ministers, with Zerahiah as their leader.

That day they offered great sacrifices and rejoiced, because the Lord had made them rejoice with great joy. The women and children also rejoiced, and the rejoicing in Jerusalem could be heard far away.

That day they gave authority to men who used to give from the treasuries to the king, over houses in which to collect the firstfruits and the tithes of the heads of the villages, as written in the book of the law, for the priests and Levites. For the Jews rejoiced over the priests and Levites who stood serving.
They kept watch in the house of their God and carried out their duties in purity, as did the ministers and gatekeepers, according to the command of David and his son Solomon.
For in David’s days Asaph lived and stood at the head of the ministers, praising and giving thanks before the Lord God.

In the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah, all Israel gave gifts to the ministers and gatekeepers, bringing them out and giving them day by day. They set apart offerings for the Levites, and the Levites set apart offerings for the sons of Aaron.
On that very day the book of the law of Moses was read aloud to the people, and it was found written in it that Ammonites and Moabites were never to enter the assembly of the Lord,
because they had not met the Israelites with bread and water, but had hired Balaam to curse them. Yet our God turned his curses into blessings.
Then, when they heard the words of the law, all those of mixed ancestry were separated from Israel.
Then Eliashib the priest came.

He built a large courtyard for him there. Previously, the offerings, frankincense, containers for the tithes of grain, wine, and oil, the firstfruits for the Levites, ministers, and gatekeepers, and the firstfruits for the priests had been kept there.
During all this I was not in Jerusalem, because in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I had gone to the king. After some time I asked the king for permission to leave.
I came to Jerusalem and learned of the evil Eliashib had done for Tobiah by making a house for him in the courtyard of the Lord.
I was greatly displeased, and I threw all the furnishings of Tobiah’s house into the street, outside the courtyard.
I gave orders, and they purified the courtyard. Then I brought back there the vessels of the Lord’s house, the offerings, and the frankincense.
I learned that the Levites’ portion was not being given to them, and that the Levites, ministers, and workers had fled, each to his own field.
I confronted the leaders and said to them, “Why has the Lord’s house been abandoned?” I gathered them together and stationed them at their posts.
All the Jews brought the tithes of grain, wine, and oil into the storehouses.

I put Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Peraiah the Levite in charge of the storehouses, and with them Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, because they were considered trustworthy. It fell to them to oversee their brothers.
Remember me, my God, for this, and do not erase the good deeds I have done in the house of my God and in carrying out its duties.

In those days I saw caravans traveling in Judah on the Sabbath, bringing loads carried on donkeys. They were also bringing wine, grapes, figs, and loads into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. I warned them, “Do not sell provisions.”
“Do not bring fish, and do not buy or sell on the Sabbath to the people of Judah in Jerusalem.”
I confronted the leaders of Judah and said to them, “Why are you doing this evil thing and profaning the Sabbath day?”
“Your ancestors did the same, and God brought all this disaster upon us and upon this city. Now you are adding fury and wrath against Israel by profaning the Sabbath day.”

Then, when the gates of Jerusalem were opened before the Sabbath, I ordered the gates to be shut. I ordered that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath, and I stationed some of my servants at the gates so that no load would enter on the Sabbath day.
The merchants and sellers of merchandise spent the night outside Jerusalem for a day or two.

I warned them and said to them, “Why do you not enter at the gate in the wall while it is still daylight? If you disregard this command, I will lay hands on you.” From that time onward they did not enter on the Sabbath.

I told the Levites to purify themselves and come in as guards and gatekeepers to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember me for this also, my God, and have compassion on me according to your abundant mercy.
Also in those days I saw Jews who had married foreign women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
Half their children spoke the language of Ashdod, and half knew how to speak Judean, but spoke the languages of the peoples.

I confronted them and cursed them. I killed some of their men and buried them. I made them swear by God, saying, “You must not give your daughters to their sons or take any of their daughters for your sons. Woe to you!”

“It was because of these things that Solomon king of Israel sinned. Among the many nations there was no king like him. He was loved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel. Yet foreign women caused even him to sin.”
“You heard the command, yet you committed this great evil, acting unfaithfully toward our God and marrying foreign women.”
One of the sons of Joiada son of Eliashib the high priest was a son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite, and I drove him away from me.
Remember them, my God, for the defilement of the priesthood and for the defilement of the priests and Levites.
I purified them from all the foreign peoples and appointed the priests and Levites to their duties, each to his own work,

and provided for the offerings and holy things at their appointed times and festivals, and for the firstfruits. Remember this good deed for me, my God. The writing of the book of Ezra the scribe is finished.
